resources.string: Add your printer to get started
Platen prints straight to your printer over Wi-Fi or a USB cable. No account, no cloud.
Documents go from this phone to your printer and nowhere else.
The IP address or host name from the printer\'s network settings page, for example 192.168.1.20, or an ipp:// address.
That does not look like an address. Use something like 192.168.1.20 or printer.local.
Could not reach the printer. Check the address, that the printer is on, and that this phone is on the same Wi-Fi.
Something answered, but not as a network printer. Check the address.
This printer only accepts encrypted connections, which Platen does not support yet.
Encrypted ipps:// addresses are not supported yet. Use the plain address of the printer.
This printer asks for a user name and password, which Platen does not support yet.
None found yet. Enter the address below if you know it.
Encrypted connections only, not supported yet
None connected. Plug the printer into the phone with a USB OTG cable.
Tap to allow access and add
Android did not allow access to the printer. Try again and choose OK.
This USB device does not offer a printer interface that Platen can use.
The printer did not answer over USB. Check that its USB port is enabled in the printer\'s settings (managed printers often have it switched off).
That file could not be read.
That PDF is password protected. Remove the password, then print it.
Platen prints PDFs and images. Export this file as a PDF from the app that made it, then print that.
That PDF could not be opened. It may be damaged.
Asking the printer what it can do…
Nothing prints on this back, but the sheet goes through the printer again with the others.
Second pass: start from the other end of the pile
Prints the backs last to first.
Your printer prints on one side only, so you turn the paper over once, halfway through: Platen prints every front, you put the pile back, then it prints every back.
1. All the fronts print, starting with page %1$s.
2. Take out the whole pile and turn it over like a book page. Keep the order.
2. Take out the whole pile and turn it over like a notepad page, top to bottom. Keep the order.
3. Put the whole pile back and continue. Page %1$s prints on the back of page %2$s.
3. Put the whole pile back and continue.
The sheet with page %1$s has nothing on its back. Put it back with the others anyway: it goes through blank so the rest line up.
Your printer turns the paper over by itself, so there is nothing for you to do.
Backs landed on the wrong sheets?
Some printers take the pile from the other end. If, with this off, page %1$s ended up on the back of page %2$s instead of page %3$s, turn it on and print again.
Some printers take the pile from the other end. If the backs came out in order but on the wrong sheets, turn this on and print again.
Backs upside down? At step 2, turn the pile over sideways like a book page, not top to bottom.
Backs upside down? At step 2, turn the pile over top to bottom like a notepad page, not sideways.
Booklets always print on both sides, turned over on the short edge.
What Platen will do with your choices on this printer
Print on one or both sides of the paper
Which pages to print, and in what order
How the pages sit on the sheet
Print whole copies one after another (1-2-3, 1-2-3) instead of page by page (1-1, 2-2, 3-3)
Automatic keeps colour only where the page has it
Only the front of each sheet is printed
Turns over on the long edge, like a book. Right for most documents.
Turns over on the short edge, upwards like a notepad or calendar.
Leave empty to print everything. Example: 1-3, 7, 10-12
For two-sided printing, use the Two-sided setting instead: Platen does the rest.
Prints the last sheet first. Turn on if your finished pile comes out back to front.
Shrinks several pages onto each sheet to save paper
Two pages per side, ordered so the folded sheets read like a book
Uses less toner or ink, lighter print
You turn the paper over: Platen prints the fronts, you put the pile back, then it prints the backs.
Copies are sent one after another so they come out in order.
The printer reports the job as finished.
The job was sent, but the printer stopped answering, so Platen cannot say how it ended. It may still print. Check the printer.
Turn the pile over and put it back
Pile is back, print the backs
2. Turn the whole pile over like a book page. Keep the order.
2. Turn the whole pile over like a notepad page, top to bottom. Keep the order.
3. Put it back in the paper tray so the printer takes the sheet with page %1$s first.
Nothing prints on the back of that sheet: it goes through blank so the others line up.
The sheet with page %1$s has nothing on its back. Put it back too: it goes through once more with nothing printed.
The sheet with page %1$s, which goes in first
The fronts are printed. Take out the whole pile, turn it over without changing the order, put it back in the paper tray, then continue.
Fronts done. Turn the pile over, put it back, then open Platen to print the backs.
Fronts done. Turn the pile over and put it back so the sheet with page %1$s goes in first, then open Platen to print the backs.
